papers.title: Deep learning-based classification of wakefulness, sleep, and rumination states in dairy cows from polysomnography and RumiWatch data.
papers.summary: Developed DairySleepNet, a deep learning framework based on selective state space models, to classify wakefulness, sleep, and rumination in dairy cows from polysomnography (PSG) and RumiWatch data. Achieved macro F1 of 86.37% and accuracy of 90.80% with PSG, but RumiWatch-only classification remained unsatisfactory, indicating that reliable on-farm sleep monitoring requires further development.

papers.title: A statistical mixture-of-experts framework for EMG artifact removal in EEG: Empirical insights and a proof-of-concept application.
papers.summary: Proposed a statistical mixture-of-experts (MoE) framework for removing electromyogenic (EMG) artifacts from single-channel EEG, leveraging insights about artifact types, specialized experts, and correlation-based objectives. Evaluated on EEGdenoiseNet (67 subjects) and SEED corpus, the MoE model achieved competitive overall denoising performance with strong lower-bound performance in high-noise settings and significant downstream classification gains.

papers.title: Seasonal variations in the polysomnographic sleep/wake cycle and activity/rest pattern in the dromedary camel (Camelus dromedarius).
papers.journal: Journal of comparative physiology. B, Biochemical, systemic, and environmental physiology
papers.summary: The study investigated seasonal variations in sleep/wake cycle and activity/rest patterns of captive dromedary camels using polysomnography and behavioral observations across four seasons. Key findings showed that in winter, total sleep time was significantly higher (4.8 h) compared to summer (3.6 h), and wakefulness percentage was lower in winter (52.9%) than summer (59.8%), with activity duration decreasing from 17.1 h in summer to 11.6 h in winter.

papers.title: A Dual Soft Attention Network for Automatic Sleep Staging via Single-Lead Electrocardiogram Signals.
papers.summary: The paper proposes SleepECGNet, a dual-attention deep learning method for automatic sleep staging using single-lead ECG signals, which extracts multi-scale features and uses SE and Luong attention to focus on relevant segments. Experiments on HMC, MGH, and SHHS1 datasets demonstrated improved classification performance, and transfer learning was applied to sleep apnea recognition.

papers.title: Brain network dynamics in the wake-sleep transition reorganize according to task engagement.
papers.summary: Used simultaneous EEG-fMRI to examine brain network dynamics during the wake-sleep transition in humans performing either an active or passive auditory task. Found that decreasing alertness led to increased parietal synchronization during passive listening, but active task engagement recruited long-range frontoparietal synchronization and auditory cortex synchronization while thalamocortical synchronization increased only during passive listening.

papers.title: Leakage-audited benchmarking reveals limited evidence for cross-subject auditory-evoked EEG vowel perception decoding.
papers.summary: Conducted a leakage-audited benchmark of cross-subject five-vowel perception decoding from auditory-evoked EEG, analyzing 1,094 epochs from 16 participants across 13 implementations. Found no significant above-chance decoding after multiplicity correction (best balanced accuracy 21.47%, chance 20%), indicating limited evidence for cross-subject vowel decoding in this dataset.

papers.title: Real-time measurement instead of prediction enables high-precision phase-specific stimulation of the human brain.
papers.summary: Developed and validated a real-time closed-loop EEG-TMS system that performs signal acquisition, phase estimation, and stimulation triggering within a 1 ms update cycle without phase prediction. In human participants across eight phases and ten frequencies (4–40 Hz), the system achieved single-digit phase accuracy, with average error 5.6°, demonstrating feasibility of prediction-free phase-specific stimulation.

papers.title: Interictal electric source imaging with open-source software and routine low-density electroencephalography: A systematic comparison of four inverse methods in drug-resistant epilepsy.
papers.summary: The study assessed interictal electrical source imaging (ESI) diagnostic accuracy using open-source software and low-density EEG with four inverse methods in drug-resistant epilepsy patients. sLORETA at the half-rising phase achieved the highest performance (accuracy 81.0%, sensitivity 82.5%, specificity 77.3%) and significantly outperformed minimum norm, with robust results across challenging subgroups.

papers.title: NEXUS-MI: Communication-Aware Federated Personalization for Gateway-Coordinated Motor-Imagery Brain-Computer Interfaces
papers.summary: NEXUS-MI introduces a gateway-coordinated federated personalization framework for EEG motor-imagery BCIs that treats synchronization as a coupled learning-and-communication control problem, with raw EEG and classifier heads kept local. Evaluated on BCICIV-2a and OpenBMI, communication-aware coordination reduced server-to-client backbone traffic by approximately 42% while cohort accuracy differences were small and realization-dependent, with subject-level losses up to 12 percentage points.

papers.title: Reduced EEG Complexity and Its Association with Social Communication in Adults with Autism Spectrum Disorder: A Multiscale Entropy Study
papers.summary: In adults with autism spectrum disorder (ASD), EEG multiscale entropy (MSE) at longer scales was reduced compared to controls across rest and movie conditions, and this reduction was associated with higher ADOS-2 Social Affect scores. Event-related MSE changes also showed attenuated differentiation between social and non-social windows in ASD.

papers.title: Frequency-aware transformer networks for robust and generalizable EEG-based seizure detection.
papers.summary: The paper introduces BrainXNet, a multi-scale spectro-temporal attention framework for EEG seizure detection. It achieves state-of-the-art accuracies of 99.1% on CHB-MIT and 98.4% on TUH, with strong cross-dataset generalization and robustness to noise, suggesting its potential for real-time clinical use.

papers.title: Talking Brains: Neonatal Aperiodic Activity in Resting State EEG Relates to Later Communicative Abilities
papers.summary: This study examined whether aperiodic activity in neonatal resting-state EEG relates to communicative abilities at 12 months in 50 typically developing infants, extracting aperiodic offset and exponent using the FOOOF algorithm. Quadratic regression showed an inverted U-shaped relationship between the neonatal aperiodic exponent and later communicative abilities, with both lower and higher exponent values associated with poorer outcomes and intermediate values with better abilities.

papers.title: Prognostic assessment of comatose patients after cardiac arrest: construction of a simplified monitoring EEG risk score across different time windows.
papers.summary: This article constructs a Simplified EEG Risk Score (SERS) for poor neurological outcome prediction in comatose patients after cardiac arrest. SERS achieved high AUCs (0.912, 0.893, 0.881) across time windows, outperforming individual EEG features and clinical predictors, offering reliable risk stratification.

papers.title: Design and validation of a modular smart headband with embroidered electrodes for comfortable EEG monitoring.
papers.summary: The study designed and validated a modular smart EEG headband with embroidered e-textile electrodes, demonstrating comparable detection of spectral and ERP effects to a commercial wet-electrode system while improving comfort and reducing skin irritation in ten healthy participants.

papers.title: Bio-inspired Terrain Perception for Snake Robots: Spectral Analysis of Vertical Undulation and Sidewinding.
papers.summary: Inspired by biological snake mechanosensation, this study proposes a proprioceptive terrain classification framework for snake robots using a single uniaxial accelerometer and a Band-Limited Spectral Magnitude feature. Validated on concrete, gravel, grass, and sand across vertical undulation and sidewinding, a hierarchical strategy achieved classification accuracies exceeding 98.8% for vertical undulation and up to 92.5% for sidewinding, with optimal frequency bands aligning with biological snake mechanoreceptor sensitivity.

papers.title: EEG-CPDD: A Covariance-Preserving Diffusion Denoiser for Reliable EEG Source Localization.
papers.journal: IEEE journal of biomedical and health informatics
papers.summary: The paper introduces EEG-CPDD, a covariance-preserving diffusion-based denoising framework for EEG source localization, which outperforms conventional denoising in preserving spatial covariance and improving source reconstruction accuracy across benchmarks.

papers.title: Neurophysiological subtyping of schizophrenia reveals a reproducible phenotype with temporoparietal circuit disruptions.
papers.summary: Using source-localized resting-state EEG functional connectivity, the authors identified two reproducible schizophrenia subtypes via sparse k-means clustering in discovery and replication cohorts; one subtype showed temporoparietal disconnection while the other had preserved connectivity, and connectivity predicted symptom severity only in the disconnected subtype.

papers.title: Closed-loop auditory stimulation in phase with slow waves during sleep enhances cerebrospinal fluid flow in humans.
papers.summary: The study developed a closed-loop auditory stimulation technique during sleep that, when aligned with slow-wave peaks, increased cerebrospinal fluid flow waves in humans, demonstrating a causal link between neural slow waves and CSF dynamics.

papers.title: Bidirectional EEG Neurofeedback of Sensorimotor Beta Oscillations Reveals Asymmetric Modulation and Strategy-Dependent Learning.
papers.summary: This exploratory double-blind sham-controlled within-subjects study tested whether 15 healthy participants could bidirectionally modulate sensorimotor beta power over C3 using EEG neurofeedback and examined learning trends. Thirteen participants successfully decreased beta activity, three successfully increased it, and two showed bidirectional control; real ENF success was significantly higher than sham only when sham was received first, indicating a transfer learning effect and strategy-dependent rather than stable plasticity.

papers.title: Neuronal Regulation and Locomotion in Rats Following Spinal Cord Injury: Reconciling Behavioral Scales With Neuroelectrophysiology.
papers.summary: This perspective evaluates the discrepancy between behavioral recovery metrics (e.g., BBB scale) and neuroelectrophysiological outcomes (MEPs/SSEPs) in rodent spinal cord injury models. It argues that relying solely on locomotor scales overestimates functional tract integrity and advocates for integrating synchronized behavioral and electrophysiological profiling to improve predictive validity in preclinical trials.

papers.title: Mapping and modulating brain dynamics in aging and neurodegeneration with electroencephalography and integrated neurotechnologies in primates.
papers.summary: This review synthesizes EEG methodologies in non-human primates (NHPs) for studying aging and neurodegeneration, highlighting EEG signatures, multimodal integration with fMRI/MEG/NIRS, and neuromodulation techniques such as TMS and tDCS. It emphasizes translational relevance for human neuroscience, including examples in Alzheimer's and Parkinson's disease models.

papers.title: Advanced imaging-integrated rTMS therapy for frontal network recovery after traumatic brain injury.
papers.summary: In a retrospective multicenter cohort study of 48 adults with traumatic brain injury, documented exposure to high-frequency left-DLPFC rTMS was associated with greater improvement in executive function scores (FAB and MoCA) and enhanced frontal-network biomarkers (N100/P200, fNIRS HbO, fMRI connectivity) compared to standard rehabilitation alone.

papers.title: Serial amplitude-integrated electroencephalography trajectories and brain-injury-associated functional immaturity in extremely preterm infants.
papers.summary: This retrospective cohort study characterized postmenstrual-age-specific Burdjalov maturation trajectories using serial amplitude-integrated EEG in 156 extremely preterm infants, comparing those with and without major brain injury. Infants with brain injury had persistently lower Burdjalov scores (e.g., 1.45 points lower at PMA 32 weeks), but the linear interaction was unstable and not reproduced by ordinal models, cautioning against interpreting it as biological recovery.

papers.title: Towards adaptive flight support: EEG-based cognitive workload monitoring in aviation scenarios.
papers.summary: In a simulated Cessna 172 flight, EEG recordings revealed phase-dependent desynchronization of alpha and beta rhythms in frontal regions during take-off, turning, and landing, and increased global efficiency and transitivity in brain networks, along with enhanced PLV and PDC connectivity, indicating higher cognitive load during demanding flight phases.

papers.title: Jogging imagery congruent with avatar gait is associated with enhanced avatar ownership during multimodal BCI control.
papers.summary: This study investigated how kinesthetic congruence between motor imagery and avatar gait affects subjective embodiment during multimodal BCI control. Participants reported significantly greater avatar ownership in the congruent (jogging imagery) condition than in the incongruent (hand-opening) condition, despite weaker MI-related SMR-ERD, suggesting that neural signal strength and embodied experience can dissociate.

papers.title: EEG-Based Auditory Attention Recognition Using DSCANet: An Innovative Incremental Learning Framework.
papers.journal: IEEE journal of biomedical and health informatics
papers.summary: The paper proposes DSCANet, an incremental learning framework for EEG-based auditory attention recognition that integrates a Dynamic Self-Organizing Convolutional Attention Network with Elastic Weight Consolidation. Under 1-second decision windows in leave-one-subject-out cross-validation, DSCANet achieved 81.51% accuracy on KUL and 63.03% on DTU, exceeding the strongest baseline by 3.41 and 6.23 percentage points, while showing improved stability against catastrophic forgetting.

papers.title: Tai Chi modulates resting alpha and theta EEG rhythms in female individuals with amphetamine-type stimulant dependence during compulsory detoxification.
papers.summary: This randomized controlled trial examined EEG alpha and theta rhythm modulation following a 6-month Tai Chi intervention versus routine physical rehabilitation in 32 female individuals with amphetamine-type stimulant dependence. Both groups showed reduced resting alpha and theta power after the intervention, while an acute bout of Tai Chi elicited higher alpha and theta power compared to treadmill exercise, suggesting distinct cortical relaxation effects.

papers.title: Modulation of fronto-parietal and autonomic activity underpins preserved working memory in middle-aged adults.
papers.summary: This study compared middle-aged high and low performers on a visuo-spatial working memory task to young adults using EEG and pupillometry. High-performing middle-aged adults exhibited prompt pupil dilation and distinct parietal alpha/beta and frontal theta event-related desynchronization during encoding and retention, suggesting that preserved working memory in midlife relies on flexible modulation of autonomic and cortical resources.

papers.title: EEGBind: Detecting Source-Level Interictal Epileptiform Discharges via EEG-Centric Multimodal Binding
papers.summary: EEGBind is an EEG-centric multimodal binding framework that uses synchronized video-context features as auxiliary evidence for five-class source-level interictal epileptiform discharge (IED) classification. On the NeuroMM 2026 Grand Challenge NMM-Source-IED benchmark, EEGBind achieved 0.8395 weighted-F1, outperforming strong competitors.

papers.title: Emotional responses to naturalistic and artificial intelligence (AI)-generated affective pictures: A systematic comparison.
papers.summary: The study compared emotional responses to AI-generated and naturalistic affective pictures by recording pupil diameter, EEG, and self-reported valence and arousal from 109 participants. Emotionally charged pictures elicited stronger responses than neutral ones for both picture types, but with weaker effect sizes for AI-generated pictures; ratings and EEG measures were strongly correlated between matched AI and original pictures.

papers.title: EEG Reactivity and Etiology as Prognostic Modifiers in Alpha and Theta Coma: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
papers.summary: This systematic review and meta-analysis of alpha/theta coma found that overall 83.7% of patients had severe disability or death, but EEG reactivity was a significant prognostic modifier: nonreactive EEG had higher odds of mortality (OR 5.67) while reactive EEG increased odds of favorable outcome (OR 8.68). Etiology also influenced outcomes.

papers.title: PQ-Neurolink: latency-aware post-quantum-ready secure communication for distributed brain-computer interfaces.
papers.summary: PQ-NeuroLink is a latency-aware post-quantum-ready communication framework that separates authenticated session establishment from symmetric streaming for distributed EEG brain-computer interfaces. In the constrained BLE 1-hop condition, hybrid ML-KEM-768 plus X25519 mode increased p95 latency by only 0.45 ms relative to the unsecured baseline while maintaining 99.0% packet delivery.

papers.title: A calculated risk: Can early EEG stratification move us toward precision post-arrest care?
papers.summary: This editorial discusses whether early EEG stratification can enable precision post-arrest care after cardiac arrest. Abstract unavailable.

papers.title: Comparative Analysis of Atrial Electrophysiology Across Animal Species and Humans: Enhancing Translation in Atrial Arrhythmia Research.
papers.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
papers.summary: This study systematically compared atrial electrophysiology across mice, rats, pigs, horses, and humans using uniform protocols. Porcine cardiomyocytes closely matched human depolarization, while early repolarization was uniquely pronounced in humans, linked to IKur expression; late repolarization scaled with cell size, and sex differences in humans were mimicked by pigs.

papers.title: Electroclinical and neuroradiological evolution in pediatric and adult patients with Rasmussen encephalitis.
papers.summary: This retrospective series of 14 pediatric and adult Rasmussen encephalitis patients found that focal motor seizures were the most common initial symptom, serial EEG progressed from focal epileptiform abnormalities to hemispheric slowing, and initial MRI frequently showed cortico-subcortical T2/FLAIR hyperintensities preceding progressive atrophy. Three patients underwent hemispherectomy, with seizure freedom achieved in two.

papers.title: Time-Frequency Analysis of Muscle Activation Patterns during the Instep Kick in Elite and Amateur Soccer Players.
papers.summary: This study compared time-frequency muscle activation patterns during the instep kick between elite and amateur soccer players using surface electromyography and Morlet wavelet analysis. Elites showed a more temporally focused pre-contact activation centered on mid-frequency components of the biceps femoris, while amateurs relied more on higher-frequency medial gastrocnemius activity during follow-through, indicating phase-specific redistributions in muscle and frequency-band activity.

papers.title: Acute catatonia and psychosis in the context of seizure exacerbation in epilepsy: a case report.
papers.summary: This case report describes a 44-year-old woman with epilepsy who developed acute catatonia and psychosis after switching from clomipramine to venlafaxine and experiencing increased seizure frequency. Management with benzodiazepines and cautious antipsychotic uptitration (quetiapine XR, cariprazine) led to complete catatonic and psychotic symptom remission over 29 days, highlighting diagnostic uncertainty, pharmacokinetic interactions, and cardiac safety considerations.

papers.title: Role Framing and Trust in Medical AI: Evidence from a Scenario Experiment and EEG.
papers.summary: This study examined how role framing (expert vs. companion) of medical AI influences trust using a scenario experiment and EEG. Expert framing increased perceived professionalism, while companion framing increased social presence, with both linked to trust, but EEG frontal-midline theta differences were exploratory and showed no behavioral trust differences, suggesting nuanced effects.

papers.title: Geographic use and performance of distributed home video-electroencephalography in Australia
papers.summary: This retrospective analysis of 3,502 home video-EEG studies in Australia found that distributed services reduced travel distance for many regional/rural patients without lowering diagnostic yield or technical performance, although remote/very remote representation was sparse and wait times longer.

papers.title: Correction: Machine learning-based lateralization and localization of seizure onset in focal cortical dysplasia patients using ictal scalp EEG.
papers.summary: This document is a published erratum correcting an earlier article on machine learning-based lateralization and localization of seizure onset in focal cortical dysplasia patients using ictal scalp EEG. It does not report new findings but serves to rectify the original publication.

topic.label: EEG & Signal Methods
topic.description: EEG signal processing, sleep staging, neural time series, modeling, and practical analysis methods.
